findings.finding: MarkdownV2 injection bypass via unescaped backslash. The `MARKDOWN_V2_SPECIALS` string does not include `\` (backslash). In Telegram MarkdownV2 `\` followed by a special char is the escape sequence, meaning a bare `\` in the output escapes the next character. If a subscriber value contains a literal `\` before any special char (e.g., value = `\*`), the escaper outputs `\` + `\*` = `\\*`. MarkdownV2 parses `\\` as a literal backslash, then `*` is bare (unescaped) and starts italic/bold formatting. Attack path: subscriber sets `first_name = "\\*injected bold text*"` and the author uses `{user.first_name}` in a MarkdownV2 message. The rendered output contains unescaped `*` which toggles bold/italic formatting, potentially injecting arbitrary Telegram markup. More severe variant: value `\\[click](https://evil.com)` — the `[` and `(` would still be individually escaped to `\\[` and `\\(`, so direct link injection is harder, but bold/italic toggling and formatting corruption are directly achievable with a single backslash.

HTML mode does not escape double-quote (`"`). The `escapeHtml` method escapes `&`, `<`, `>` but not `"`. If an author writes a template with an HTML attribute containing a subscriber-controlled value — for example `link` — a subscriber value containing `"` could break out of the attribute context. Example: `custom.website = 'http://x.com" onclick="alert(1)'` yields `link`. While Telegram strips most event handlers and JavaScript in its HTML parser, and the Telegram HTML subset is very limited, leaving `"` unescaped is against the principle of defense-in-depth for injection prevention. The spec (Decision 10) says values must be escaped per mode rules; the HTML spec requires `"` → `"` in attribute values.

The `markdownV2ModeEscapesFullCharset` test does not include `\\` (backslash) in the test payload `"_*[]()~\`>#+-=|{}.!"`, so it does not verify that backslash is escaped. This means the critical backslash injection finding (above) is undetected by the test suite.
findings.recommendation: Extend the test payload to include a backslash and assert it is doubled: value `"\\<special>"` should render as `"\\\\\\<escaped-special>"`. Add a dedicated test: `markdownV2EscapesBackslash()` that verifies `\\` → `\\\\` in the output.

findings.finding: The `indexOf('}', i + 1)` search for the closing brace does not skip over `}}` (escaped braces) when scanning forward for the closing `}`. Consider a template like `{user.first_name}}` — the parser finds `{` at position 0, then `indexOf('}', 1)` finds the first `}` at position 16 (end of `first_name`), extracts key `user.first_name`, then `}}` at positions 17-18 is processed in the next iteration as an escaped `}` literal. This produces `Ada}` — the trailing `}}` becomes one literal `}`. This is arguably correct behavior (the `}}` after the closing `}` is a standalone `}}` escape), but it is counterintuitive and undocumented. More subtly, the template `{cus}tom.key}` would resolve key `cus` (unknown → empty), then emit `tom.key}` verbatim. This is correct for the single-pass design, but should be covered by a test to lock down the behavior.
findings.recommendation: Document this behavior explicitly in the class Javadoc and add a test case covering `{key}}` (closing double-brace after placeholder) to ensure the behavior is stable and intentional.

summary: One critical injection bypass: MarkdownV2 mode does not escape the backslash character (`\`), allowing a subscriber with a crafted value (e.g., `\*`) to produce an unescaped MarkdownV2 special character in the output and inject bold/italic formatting. Fix: add `\` to the escaped character set, handled before other specials. One major finding: HTML mode omits double-quote escaping, enabling attribute breakout if an author embeds a subscriber value in an `href` or other attribute. Two minor findings: the test suite does not cover the backslash case, and the brace-scanning behavior around `}}` after a placeholder is undocumented. The PII/logging requirement (Decision 16) is correctly implemented — no rendered values or field values are logged. Order-of-operations is correct: escaping is applied after resolution and only to values, before insertion into the output; the single-pass design prevents second-order injection. The `renderValue` type-rendering logic (Double/Instant/Boolean) is correct and does not introduce injection surface.
